# Liberal Democrats 2024 Manifesto Summary

## Economy and Business
The manifesto proposes managing public finances to reduce national debt as a share of GDP while investing in infrastructure. Key measures include replacing business rates with a Commercial Landowner Levy, expanding the British Business Bank, and creating Lifelong Skills Grants of £5,000 for adult education. The party would reform capital gains tax, increase the Digital Services Tax to 6%, and introduce a 4% tax on FTSE-100 share buybacks. Trade policy focuses on reducing barriers with European partners through veterinary agreements and mutual recognition arrangements.

## Health and Social Care
The NHS plan includes recruiting 8,000 additional GPs to enable seven-day appointment guarantees, establishing mental health hubs for young people, and guaranteeing cancer treatment within 62 days of referral. Social care would be reformed through free personal care (modelled on Scotland's system), a £2/hour increase to care worker minimum wage, and a cross-party commission on long-term funding. Unpaid carers would receive increased Carer's Allowance and statutory respite breaks.

## Environment and Energy
Climate targets include net zero by 2045 and 90% renewable electricity by 2030. A ten-year home insulation programme would prioritise low-income households. Water companies would face sewage discharge bans, bonus restrictions, and potential transformation into public benefit companies. Tree planting targets are set at 60 million annually, with legally binding nature recovery targets.

## Housing and Planning
Housing construction targets are 380,000 homes annually, including 150,000 social homes. Measures include ten new garden cities, land compensation reform, and abolishing residential leasehold. Renters would gain three-year default tenancies and no-fault eviction bans. Local authorities would receive powers to control second homes and short-term lets.

## Education
Proposals include a qualified mental health professional in every school, above-inflation funding increases, and free school meals for all children in poverty. Teacher recruitment would be supported through independent pay review and funded training. Higher education changes include reinstating maintenance grants and reviewing the financing system.

## Immigration and Asylum
The manifesto proposes replacing salary thresholds with merit-based work visas, expanding Youth Mobility Schemes, and reversing family visa income threshold increases. Asylum processing would target three-month decisions, with asylum seekers permitted to work after three months. The Rwanda scheme would be cancelled, with resources redirected to backlog clearance.

## Political Reform
Electoral changes include proportional representation via Single Transferable Vote for MPs and English councillors, votes at 16, and abolishing voter ID requirements. The Ministerial Code would become statutory, donation caps would be introduced, and House of Lords reform would proceed. A federal UK structure is proposed with enhanced devolution.

## Defence and International
Defence spending would increase toward 2.5% of GDP, with Army cuts reversed. The nuclear deterrent would be maintained. European relations would follow a four-stage roadmap toward Single Market membership. Ukraine support would continue, including seizure of frozen Russian assets. International development spending would return to 0.7% of national income.
